knowledge:
- key_parameters: bamdir=Vector indicating the directories of all .bam files ;; bedFile=Directory of the .bed file (WES bait file, no header, sorted by start and end positions) ;; chr=Chromosome to process (CODEX processes the genome chromosome by chromosome) ;; mapqthres=Mapping quality threshold to filter reads in getcoverage (default is 20) ;; cov_thresh=Exon-wise coverage threshold vector in qc to filter out low/high coverage exons ;; length_thresh=Exon length threshold vector in qc to filter exons by length ;; mapp_thresh=Mappability threshold in qc to filter out low-mappability exons ;; gc_thresh=GC content percentage threshold vector in qc to filter exons ;; K=Range of latent factors to fit in normalize/normalize2 ;; normal_index=Indices of normal/control samples when using normalize2 in a case-control design ;; mode=Segmentation mode in segment, set to "integer" for germline CNV detection or "fraction" for somatic CNV detection in mixed populations ;; lmax=Maximum length of CNV in terms of number of exons in segment (default is 200)
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use this package when calling copy number variations (CNVs) from whole exome sequencing (WES) data across multiple samples processed using the same sequencing pipeline. It is appropriate for both germline CNV detection and somatic CNV detection in mixed/cancer populations, and does not require matched controls (though it can utilize them if available).
- pitfalls: Ensure that chromosome formats are completely consistent between the .bed and .bam files. Over-normalization can remove true CNV signals which cannot be recovered post-normalization; therefore, CODEX recommends choosing a conservative (smaller) value of K when in doubt. For the "fraction" mode, post-segmentation thresholding is necessary to filter out long CNV events with fractional copy numbers close to 2.

workflows.name: standard_wes_cnv_calling
workflows.intent: Call copy number variations (CNVs) from whole exome sequencing (WES) data using a standard multi-sample cohort without matched controls.
input: *.bam (BAM files containing aligned WES reads for multiple samples)
*.bed (WES bait/target file containing exon coordinates, sorted, no header)
sampname (text file containing sample names, one per row)
workflows.stages: 1. Load BAM and BED files using getbambed ;; 2. Compute raw read depth coverage using getcoverage ;; 3. Retrieve GC content and mappability using getgc and getmapp ;; 4. Perform quality control filtering on exons and samples using qc ;; 5. Fit Poisson latent factor model for normalization using normalize ;; 6. Determine the optimal number of latent factors (K) using choiceofK ;; 7. Run Poisson log-likelihood ratio-based segmentation to call CNVs using segment
workflows.code:
library(CODEX)
library(WES.1KG.WUGSC) # Load Toy data from the 1000 Genomes Project.
dirPath <- system.file("extdata", package = "WES.1KG.WUGSC")
bamFile <- list.files(dirPath, pattern = '*.bam$')
bamdir <- file.path(dirPath, bamFile)
sampname <- as.matrix(read.table(file.path(dirPath, "sampname")))
bedFile <- file.path(dirPath, "chr22_400_to_500.bed")
chr <- 22
bambedObj <- getbambed(bamdir = bamdir, bedFile = bedFile, 
                       sampname = sampname, projectname = "CODEX_demo", chr)
bamdir <- bambedObj$bamdir; sampname <- bambedObj$sampname
ref <- bambedObj$ref; projectname <- bambedObj$projectname; chr <- bambedObj$chr
coverageObj <- getcoverage(bambedObj, mapqthres = 20)
Y <- coverageObj$Y; readlength <- coverageObj$readlength
gc <- getgc(chr, ref)
mapp <- getmapp(chr, ref)
qcObj <- qc(Y, sampname, chr, ref, mapp, gc, cov_thresh = c(20, 4000), 
    length_thresh = c(20, 2000), mapp_thresh = 0.9, gc_thresh = c(20, 80))
Y_qc <- qcObj$Y_qc; sampname_qc <- qcObj$sampname_qc; gc_qc <- qcObj$gc_qc
mapp_qc <- qcObj$mapp_qc; ref_qc <- qcObj$ref_qc; qcmat <- qcObj$qcmat
write.table(qcmat, file = paste(projectname, '_', chr, '_qcmat', '.txt', sep=''),
            sep='\t', quote=FALSE, row.names=FALSE)
normObj <- normalize(Y_qc, gc_qc, K = 1:9)
Yhat <- normObj$Yhat; AIC <- normObj$AIC; BIC <- normObj$BIC
RSS <- normObj$RSS; K <- normObj$K
choiceofK(AIC, BIC, RSS, K, filename = paste(projectname, "_", chr, 
    "_choiceofK", ".pdf", sep = ""))
optK = K[which.max(BIC)]
finalcall <- segment(Y_qc, Yhat, optK = optK, K = K, sampname_qc,
    ref_qc, chr, lmax = 200, mode = "integer")
finalcall
write.table(finalcall, file = paste(projectname, '_', chr, '_', optK,
            '_CODEX_frac.txt', sep=''), sep='\t', quote=FALSE, row.names=FALSE)
save.image(file = paste(projectname, '_', chr, '_image', '.rda', sep=''),
     compress='xz')

workflows.name: case_control_wes_cnv_calling
workflows.intent: Call copy number variations (CNVs) from whole exome sequencing (WES) data under a case-control design, estimating latent factors from control samples.
input: *.bam (BAM files containing aligned WES reads for case and control samples)
*.bed (WES bait/target file containing exon coordinates, sorted, no header)
sampname (text file containing sample names, one per row)
workflows.stages: 1. Load BAM and BED files using getbambed ;; 2. Compute raw read depth coverage using getcoverage ;; 3. Retrieve GC content and mappability using getgc and getmapp ;; 4. Perform quality control filtering on exons and samples using qc ;; 5. Fit Poisson latent factor model using control samples for normalization via normalize2 ;; 6. Determine the optimal number of latent factors (K) using choiceofK ;; 7. Run Poisson log-likelihood ratio-based segmentation to call CNVs using segment
workflows.code:
library(CODEX)
library(WES.1KG.WUGSC) # Load Toy data from the 1000 Genomes Project.
dirPath <- system.file("extdata", package = "WES.1KG.WUGSC")
bamFile <- list.files(dirPath, pattern = '*.bam$')
bamdir <- file.path(dirPath, bamFile)
sampname <- as.matrix(read.table(file.path(dirPath, "sampname")))
bedFile <- file.path(dirPath, "chr22_400_to_500.bed")
chr <- 22
bambedObj <- getbambed(bamdir = bamdir, bedFile = bedFile, 
                       sampname = sampname, projectname = "CODEX_demo", chr)
bamdir <- bambedObj$bamdir; sampname <- bambedObj$sampname
ref <- bambedObj$ref; projectname <- bambedObj$projectname; chr <- bambedObj$chr
coverageObj <- getcoverage(bambedObj, mapqthres = 20)
Y <- coverageObj$Y; readlength <- coverageObj$readlength
gc <- getgc(chr, ref)
mapp <- getmapp(chr, ref)
qcObj <- qc(Y, sampname, chr, ref, mapp, gc, cov_thresh = c(20, 4000), 
    length_thresh = c(20, 2000), mapp_thresh = 0.9, gc_thresh = c(20, 80))
Y_qc <- qcObj$Y_qc; sampname_qc <- qcObj$sampname_qc; gc_qc <- qcObj$gc_qc
mapp_qc <- qcObj$mapp_qc; ref_qc <- qcObj$ref_qc; qcmat <- qcObj$qcmat
write.table(qcmat, file = paste(projectname, '_', chr, '_qcmat', '.txt', sep=''),
            sep='\t', quote=FALSE, row.names=FALSE)
normObj <- normalize2(Y_qc, gc_qc, K = 1:9, normal_index=seq(1,45,2))
Yhat <- normObj$Yhat; AIC <- normObj$AIC; BIC <- normObj$BIC
RSS <- normObj$RSS; K <- normObj$K
choiceofK(AIC, BIC, RSS, K, filename = paste(projectname, "_", chr, 
    "_choiceofK", ".pdf", sep = ""))
optK = K[which.max(BIC)]
finalcall <- segment(Y_qc, Yhat, optK = optK, K = K, sampname_qc,
    ref_qc, chr, lmax = 200, mode = "integer")
finalcall
write.table(finalcall, file = paste(projectname, '_', chr, '_', optK,
            '_CODEX_frac.txt', sep=''), sep='\t', quote=FALSE, row.names=FALSE)
save.image(file = paste(projectname, '_', chr, '_image', '.rda', sep=''),
     compress='xz')
